# Delivery routing ruling (e2e synthetic)

Tanya (team owner) ruled on where reaction delivery belongs:

> we route every reaction through one bundle per run per person, not one
> message per skill — a person should get one thing to read, not four

Tina pushed back on the batching window and Tanya held: the bundle closes when
the run closes, and a skill that misses the close waits for the next run rather
than sending on its own. The alternative considered and rejected was per-skill
delivery with client-side collapsing, which moves the ordering problem onto the
reader.

payload.rationale: I called perspective once and checked the map, coverage, Thematic and Documents doors. The graph is centred on Teamwork's decision-capture product (anti-Slack positioning, decisions evaporating in chat, context preservation, webhook architecture), and no area covers reaction delivery, bundling, or batching windows, so the document has no direct home in it. I expanded the nearest frames: the anti-Slack narrative and its real-time-chat anti-pattern position (one bundle versus a stream of messages), the decisions-evaporate narrative, the context-preservation position, and the webhook architecture position (process only what matters, not every message). I deliberately did not expand pricing, target market, or product-category positions, which do not bear on delivery routing. The document is a synthetic e2e ruling, so the passes should treat any link to these positions as weak.

placements.why: The position's members decide that delivery is bundled per run per person. A person should get one thing to read, not four. The bundle closes with the run, and per-skill delivery with client-side collapsing is rejected because it moves the ordering problem onto the reader. That is a standing theme about delivery shape that future rulings (windows, routing, collapsing) will keep feeding. No existing leaf holds it. Narrative_DecisionsEvaporate is about decisions disappearing in real-time chat, and nothing in these members concerns that. Narrative_AntiSlackPositioning is the nearest relation: it favors structured delivery over noise, so it is linked with 'see' rather than reused.
